h1: SkyElite Private Jets — Travel Hero Section Design
tagline: “Your dedication deserves recognition” — the whole hero section is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Hero section reference for a travel brand — React and Tailwind CSS, #1A2229 base, Inter and a 1920x1455 frame.
about: SkyElite Private Jets gives a travel brand a finished first screen and the numbers that produced it. The headline reads “Your dedication deserves recognition”, and the rest of the hero section is arranged around it. Colour is limited to deep blue #1A2229 underneath, set in Inter. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 1920x1455 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. If you are briefing a travel hero section, start from this composition and replace the subject.

layout.title: Links collapse at one width
layout.body: The bar is one row of text and one action, measured at 100vh sections and 12px spacing steps so it reads as a strip rather than as a band. The bar sits over the 1920x1455 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: One family, two roles
layout.body: Typography is Inter, and the brief assigns the face a job rather than mixing for variety. Weight, tracking and size steps are all specified, so the hierarchy survives a substitution. The face is paired with fixed sizes, which is what keeps the display line and the interface text related.

layout.title: Navigation held to one row
layout.body: Labels are short enough to stay on one line at every width the brief covers. Copy this pattern when you need navigation that survives a loud first screen.

layout.title: One scale for type and frame
layout.body: Sizes are quoted rather than inherited: 100vh sections and 12px spacing steps. Swap the face or the copy and those relationships still hold. Each value maps to one job: a type step, a gap, a radius or a transition.

motion.title: Feedback on the controls
motion.body: States are handled per component (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card) rather than by a global animation layer. Interactive targets are large enough to tap and the pointer treatment is consistent across them. A few reliable states beat a long list of effects.

motion.title: Almost no motion
motion.body: The brief leaves animation out and lets the 1920x1455 layout carry the page, with hover and press states the only changes. Only the elements that respond to the pointer move. Keep motion to the controls.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

editorial.title: How the hero section reflows
editorial.body: Where a template collapses to a single column and hopes, this brief states what happens (the section is held at 100vh and the navigation collapses into a mobile menu) and keeps the order intact. Both states are described in the same brief.

editorial.title: Making the hero section yours
editorial.body: The brief names Inter and the scale beside it. Substitute a face with the same proportions and the composition survives. Substitution is cheaper than composition, and that is the point.

editorial.title: Reading SkyElite Private Jets as a spec
editorial.body: Committing to 100vh sections and 12px spacing steps trades flexibility for repeatability. That is the point of the reference: the same page in a different brand, without a new set of guesses. Nothing in this hero section depends on a default.

faq.question: What do I get when I copy the SkyElite Private Jets brief?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1920x1455, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: How much of SkyElite Private Jets depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: SkyElite Private Jets was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Can I use SkyElite Private Jets in a client project?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 1920x1455.
